expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "there's a window where old instances SELECT legacy_email against a schema that no longer has it — errors on every request through those three paths."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "Today: merge the code change... Next week: separate PR, just the migration, after the code has soaked in prod."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "Nothing in the PR restores it — not a revert, not a redeploy. The only restore path is a database point-in-time restore."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Code-only: minutes, and one person can do it. With the DROP: hours, needs someone with restore access, and Friday evening is when that person is least likely to be reachable."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "Friday evening is when that person is least likely to be reachable."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "a CI check blocking destructive DDL in the same change as application code. Want me to write one for your repo?"

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "Today: merge the code change... hold the DROP."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "Fully revertible, safe to ship Friday" vs the DROP which is not.
